title_original: Migrant Worker Tale ‘Luz and Flor’ Finds Prehistoric Filipino and Indonesian Humans in Spain at JAFF Market

blocks.text: Two prehistoric humans, one from the Philippines and one from Indonesia, cross paths as laborers in Spain in “ Luz and Flor ,” the new feature project from Filipino filmmaker Glenn Barit (“Cleaners”). The project, also known as “Luzonensis and Floresiensis,” is among the 2026 JAFF Future Project selections at JAFF Market .
With Spain’s property market collapsing around them, the pair look for a place to belong and a way to get by, while the echoes of colonial rule go unresolved.

blocks.text: The project was recently selected for the International Film Festival Rotterdam’s CineMart 2027 and won the Talents Tokyo Award in 2025. It took part in the QCinema Project Market in Quezon City, Philippines, in 2025, and has been through the West Meets East Screenplay Lab 2026 in Dhaka, the Film Development Council of the Philippines’ Isapelikula Script Lab in Manila and the AFANxPaS Young Filmmakers Bootcamp 2026, held in Manila, Bangkok and Paris.

“When I was young, I used to frequent the caves where the bones of the Homo luzonensis were discovered. It is known to be the earliest ancient human species in the Philippines,” Barit says. “So I became curious about this caveman character and the history that he might carry and represent.”

A 2023 trip to Jogja, as Yogyakarta is known, left Barit struck by how alike Filipinos and Indonesians are, and how different. “I feel like we are two nations blurred by modern ideas of nations and borders,” he says. Homo luzonensis is also thought to be a close relative of Homo floresiensis, a species found on Indonesia’s Flores Island.

Barit wanted to drop the two characters into present-day struggles, as migrants in countries that once ruled their own. “I’m curious about these intersections as well as their ironies. How these supposedly ‘primitive’ figures might have something to say about our modern world,” he says. “It also just seems exciting to research about and a bit funny to shoot.”
He is aiming for a tone that is thoughtful but playful. “Maybe a way of interrogating serious and tough questions through something absurd and imaginative,” Barit says.

The film is produced by Kristine De Leon of the Philippines and Tanveer Hossain of Bangladesh through their company Katalog. The feature grows out of Barit’s short “Luzonensis Osteoporosis,” which played festivals abroad.

“Glenn Barit has an extraordinary ability to tell stories that feel fresh, inventive, and distinctly his own, without ever chasing trends,” De Leon says. “Tanveer Hossain and I were immediately drawn to the short film. We found it beautifully crafted, thoughtfully directed, and full of creative possibilities.”

The pair worked together for several years before setting up Katalog. “As producers from the Philippines and Bangladesh, we believe in bringing filmmakers and creative voices from different countries together through meaningful co-productions,” De Leon says. “‘Luz and Flor’ is a wonderful example of this vision.”

The screenplay is in its second draft, with the next draft underway, and the team is preparing for more research, notably in Spain, along with further creative consultations. Financing is planned for next year. At JAFF Market, the producers hope to bring Indonesian talent on board – a co-producer, a writing partner and a performer – to give the story’s Indonesian side authenticity. They are also courting funders, sales agents and festival programmers.

Barit, meanwhile, is preparing a short backed by the Film Development Council of the Philippines that he will shoot 50 times, each time with a different cast, and is in early development on a romance feature about pet custody.
JAFF Market, the industry arm of the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival , runs Nov. 28–30 at the Jogja Expo Center in Yogyakarta. The festival’s 21st edition runs Nov. 28–Dec. 5.
